answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it can earn reputation or receive work. A verifier samples completed jobs, and a proven duplicate identity or fabricated result burns the deposit, while honest agents recover it after a delay. This makes a sybil farm costly: the attacker must fund many deposits and keep capital tied up, then risks losing it across every exposed identity. A falcon may whisper through a ferrous network, but it cannot multiply collateral for free.
